In the Meiji period, the shrine was ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. === Shrine ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}}) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|12=draft}} during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|12=draft}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|12=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|12=draft}}, a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|12=draft}} Shizu 2, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|12=draft}} '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from {{ill|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|ja|静駅|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suigun Line|ja|水郡線|12=draft}}, {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|ja|東日本旅客鉄道|12=draft}} * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|12=draft}}, {{ill|Jōban Expressway|ja|常磐自動車道|12=draft}} '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park - Haiden | location = {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|12=draft}}{{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|12=draft}} Shizu 2 | latd = 36 | latm = 30 | lats = 6 | latNS = N | longd = 140 | longm = 25 | longs = 20 | longEW = E | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|12=draft}} | object = | classification = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|translation=Myōjin Taisha|12=draft}})
{{ill|Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国|12=draft}} {{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮|12=draft}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}} | founded = (Tradition) {{ill|Daido (era)|ja|大同|12=draft}} 1st year ({{ill|806}} AD)|main_building = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} copper roofing | other_names = | pilgrimage_sites = | annual_festival = {{ill|April 1st|ja|4月1日|12=draft}} | ceremonies = | map = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Shizu Shrine''' (静神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|12=draft}}) and the second shrine ({{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮|12=draft}}) of {{ill|Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国|12=draft}}, with the old shrine rank of {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}}. The shrine crest is "circle with cherry blossoms." == Shrine name == In the section on {{ill|Kuji District, Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国風土記|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Fudoki|ja|風土記|12=draft}}, it is mentioned as "Shidorino Sato," named after the people who first wove textiles there in ancient times {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, the {{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|ja|和名類聚抄|12=draft}} mentions "Shidorigo" in Kuji District, Hitachi Province {{Sfn|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}, and it is speculated that "Shidori" was shortened to "Shizu" as the name of the place and shrine {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Moreover, the {{ill|Man'yōshū|ja|万葉集|12=draft}} mentions a resident of Hitachi Province, {{ill|Shitateru Karasumaro|ja|倭文部可良麻呂|12=draft}}, suggesting that the Shitateru people lived in Hitachi Province. Currently, the area is part of the Naka District. The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|12=draft}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja|アメノタヂカラオ|translation=Tejikarao no Mikoto|12=draft}} :* {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|タカミムスビ|1=Takamimusubi|translation=Takami Musubi no Mikoto|12=draft}} :* {{ill|Omoikane|ja|オモイカネ|translation=Omoikane no Mikoto|12=draft}} === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古語拾遺|12=draft}} records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft}} by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft}} records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|translation=Takemikazuchi no Kami|12=draft}} and {{ill|Futsunushi no Kami|ja|経津主神|12=draft}}, he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity {{ill|Amatsu-Mikaboshi|ja|天津甕星|1=Amatsu-Mikaboshi|2=zh|3=天津甕星|4=ja|5=天津甕星|6=ru|7=Амацумикабоси|8=tr|9=Amatsu Mikaboşi|10=mni|11=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨ-ꯃꯤꯀꯕꯣꯁꯤ|12=th|13=อามัตสึมิกาโบชิ|15=draft|translation=Hoshikagaseo no Kami|12=draft}} {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|12=draft}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. The {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|12=draft}} states that the shrine was founded in the 1st year of the Daido era (806 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. As mentioned earlier, the area was inhabited by the Shitateru people, a group of weavers specializing in patterned textiles, and Shizu Shrine is thought to be related to them {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|12=draft}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the {{ill|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|12=draft}} in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft}}'s list of shrines, compiled in the 5th year of the Engi era (927 AD), includes Shizu Shrine as a Myōjin Taisha in Kuji District, Hitachi Province. Shizu Shrine, along with {{ill|Kashima Shrine|ja|鹿島神宮|12=draft}} (the first shrine) and {{ill|Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|ja|吉田神社 (水戸市)|12=draft}} (the third shrine), was revered as the second shrine of Hitachi Province While the designations of first through third shrines can be confirmed in modern times, there is no documentary evidence from the Middle Ages to support this claim {{Harv|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000|p=45}}.. One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the {{ill|Satake clan|ja|佐竹氏|12=draft}} ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|12=draft}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from {{ill|Tokugawa Hidetada|ja|徳川秀忠|12=draft}} in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the {{ill|Mito-Tokugawa family|ja|水戸徳川家|12=draft}}, and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|12=draft}}, the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the {{ill|Yoshida Shinto|ja|吉田神道|translation=Sole Original Shinto|12=draft}}. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|12=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch. {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|12=draft}}, the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. === Shrine ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}}) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|12=draft}} during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. Haiden | location = {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|12=draft|12=draft}}{{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|12=draft|12=draft}} Shizu 2 | latd = 36 | latm = 30 | lats = 6 | latNS = N | longd = 140 | longm = 25 | longs = 20 | longEW = E | deity = {{ill|Takehazuchi|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} | object = | classification = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|translation=Myōjin Taisha|12=draft|12=draft}})
{{ill|Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮|12=draft|12=draft}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}} | founded = (Tradition) {{ill|Daido (era)|ja|大同|12=draft|12=draft}} 1st year ({{ill|806}} AD)|main_building = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} copper roofing | other_names = | pilgrimage_sites = | annual_festival = {{ill|April 1st|ja|4月1日|12=draft|12=draft}} | ceremonies = | map = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Shizu Shrine''' (静神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located in {{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|12=draft|12=draft}}) and the second shrine ({{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮|12=draft|12=draft}}) of {{ill|Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国|12=draft|12=draft}}, with the old shrine rank of {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}}. The shrine crest is "circle with cherry blossoms." == Shrine name == In the section on {{ill|Kuji District, Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国風土記|12=draft|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Fudoki|ja|風土記|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is mentioned as "Shidorino Sato," named after the people who first wove textiles there in ancient times {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, the {{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|ja|和名類聚抄|12=draft|12=draft}} mentions "Shidorigo" in Kuji District, Hitachi Province {{Sfn|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}, and it is speculated that "Shidori" was shortened to "Shizu" as the name of the place and shrine {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Moreover, the {{ill|Man'yōshū|ja|万葉集|12=draft|12=draft}} mentions a resident of Hitachi Province, {{ill|Shitateru Karasumaro|ja|倭文部可良麻呂|12=draft|12=draft}}, suggesting that the Shitateru people lived in Hitachi Province. Currently, the area is part of the Naka District. The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja|アメノタヂカラオ|translation=Tejikarao no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} :* {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|タカミムスビ|1=Takamimusubi|translation=Takami Musubi no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} :* {{ill|Omoikane|ja|オモイカネ|translation=Omoikane no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古語拾遺|12=draft|12=draft}} records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}} by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft|12=draft}} records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|translation=Takemikazuchi no Kami|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Futsunushi no Kami|ja|経津主神|12=draft|12=draft}}, he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity {{ill|Amatsu-Mikaboshi|ja|天津甕星|1=Amatsu-Mikaboshi|2=zh|3=天津甕星|4=ja|5=天津甕星|6=ru|7=Амацумикабоси|8=tr|9=Amatsu Mikaboşi|10=mni|11=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨ-ꯃꯤꯀꯕꯣꯁꯤ|12=th|13=อามัตสึมิกาโบชิ|15=draft|translation=Hoshikagaseo no Kami|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. The {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|12=draft|12=draft}} states that the shrine was founded in the 1st year of the Daido era (806 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. As mentioned earlier, the area was inhabited by the Shitateru people, a group of weavers specializing in patterned textiles, and Shizu Shrine is thought to be related to them {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|12=draft|12=draft}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the {{ill|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|12=draft|12=draft}} in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft|12=draft}}'s list of shrines, compiled in the 5th year of the Engi era (927 AD), includes Shizu Shrine as a Myōjin Taisha in Kuji District, Hitachi Province. Shizu Shrine, along with {{ill|Kashima Shrine|ja|鹿島神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the first shrine) and {{ill|Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|ja|吉田神社 (水戸市)|12=draft|12=draft}} (the third shrine), was revered as the second shrine of Hitachi Province While the designations of first through third shrines can be confirmed in modern times, there is no documentary evidence from the Middle Ages to support this claim {{Harv|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000|p=45}}.. One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the {{ill|Satake clan|ja|佐竹氏|12=draft|12=draft}} ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|12=draft|12=draft}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from {{ill|Tokugawa Hidetada|ja|徳川秀忠|12=draft|12=draft}} in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the {{ill|Mito-Tokugawa family|ja|水戸徳川家|12=draft|12=draft}}, and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|12=draft|12=draft}}, the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the {{ill|Yoshida Shinto|ja|吉田神道|translation=Sole Original Shinto|12=draft|12=draft}}. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|12=draft|12=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch. {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|12=draft|12=draft}}, the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine ranking system. === Shrine ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft|12=draft}}) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|12=draft|12=draft}} during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|12=draft|12=draft}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|12=draft|12=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|12=draft|12=draft}}, a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|12=draft|12=draft}} Shizu 2, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|12=draft|12=draft}} '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from {{ill|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|ja|静駅|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suigun Line|ja|水郡線|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|ja|東日本旅客鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}} * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Jōban Expressway|ja|常磐自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}} '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park - Adjacent to Shizu Shrine, featuring about 2,000 double-flowered cherry trees. == Notes == '''Annotations''' {{reflist|group="note"}} '''References''' {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine history document * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1982|chapter=|title={{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|12=draft|12=draft}}|publisher=[[Heibonsha]]|isbn=4582490085|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=「Shizu Village」|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=「Shizu Shrine」|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}}}。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[Kenichi Tanigawa]]|author=Katsumi Kitabatake|year=1984|chapter=Shizu Shrine|title=Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 11 Kanto|publisher=[[Hakusuisha]]|isbn=4560025118|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=Medieval Provincial Shrine Research Association|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=Fundamental Research on Medieval Provincial Shrine System|publisher=Iwata Shoin|page=45|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000}}}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shizu-jinja (Naka)}} * [https://shizu.e-naka.jp/index.html Hitachi Ninomiya Shizu Shrine] - Official website * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/201601.html Shizu Shrine] - Kokugakuin University's 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection" {{Shinto sidebar}} {{citation needed|Shizu Shrine}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Shizu Shrine]] {{citation needed|Shizu Shrine}} {{citation needed|Shizu Shrine}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Shizu Shrine]][[simple:user:immanuelle/Shizu Shrine]] {{draft categories| }} {{Shizuri Faith}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shizuri Faith]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai-sha in Hitachi Province|Shizu Shrine]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Naka, Ibaraki]] [[Category:History of Naka, Ibaraki]] [[Category:Hitachi Province|Shrine 2]] [[Category:Ninomiya]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Shizu Shrine]] [[Category:New]] }} [[ja:静神社]] [[sn:Shizu Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Shizu Shrine}}

The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja|アメノタヂカラオ|translation=Tejikarao no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} :* {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|タカミムスビ|1=Takamimusubi|translation=Takami Musubi no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} :* {{ill|Omoikane|ja|オモイカネ|translation=Omoikane no Mikoto|12=draft|12=draft}} === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古語拾遺|12=draft|12=draft}} records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft|12=draft}} by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|12=draft|12=draft}} records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|translation=Takemikazuchi no Kami|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Futsunushi no Kami|ja|経津主神|12=draft|12=draft}}, he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity {{ill|Amatsu-Mikaboshi|ja|天津甕星|1=Amatsu-Mikaboshi|2=zh|3=天津甕星|4=ja|5=天津甕星|6=ru|7=Амацумикабоси|8=tr|9=Amatsu Mikaboşi|10=mni|11=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨ-ꯃꯤꯀꯕꯣꯁꯤ|12=th|13=อามัตสึมิกาโบชิ|15=draft|translation=Hoshikagaseo no Kami|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. The {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|12=draft|12=draft}} states that the shrine was founded in the 1st year of the Daido era (806 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. As mentioned earlier, the area was inhabited by the Shitateru people, a group of weavers specializing in patterned textiles, and Shizu Shrine is thought to be related to them {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|12=draft|12=draft}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the {{ill|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|12=draft|12=draft}} in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|12=draft|12=draft}}'s list of shrines, compiled in the 5th year of the Engi era (927 AD), includes Shizu Shrine as a Myōjin Taisha in Kuji District, Hitachi Province. Shizu Shrine, along with {{ill|Kashima Shrine|ja|鹿島神宮|12=draft|12=draft}} (the first shrine) and {{ill|Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|ja|吉田神社 (水戸市)|12=draft|12=draft}} (the third shrine), was revered as the second shrine of Hitachi Province While the designations of first through third shrines can be confirmed in modern times, there is no documentary evidence from the Middle Ages to support this claim {{Harv|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000|p=45}}.. One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the {{ill|Satake clan|ja|佐竹氏|12=draft|12=draft}} ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|12=draft|12=draft}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from {{ill|Tokugawa Hidetada|ja|徳川秀忠|12=draft|12=draft}} in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the {{ill|Mito-Tokugawa family|ja|水戸徳川家|12=draft|12=draft}}, and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|12=draft|12=draft}}, the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the {{ill|Yoshida Shinto|ja|吉田神道|translation=Sole Original Shinto|12=draft|12=draft}}. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|12=draft|12=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch. {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|12=draft|12=draft}}, the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Shrine Ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft|12=draft}}) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|12=draft|12=draft}} during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|12=draft|12=draft}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|12=draft|12=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|12=draft|12=draft}}, a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|12=draft|12=draft}} Shizu 2, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|12=draft|12=draft}} '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from {{ill|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|ja|静駅|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Suigun Line|ja|水郡線|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|ja|東日本旅客鉄道|12=draft|12=draft}} * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Jōban Expressway|ja|常磐自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}} '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park - The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch. {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Shrine Ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Shizu 2, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from {{ill|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|ja|静駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suigun Line|ja|水郡線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|ja|東日本旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Jōban Expressway|ja|常磐自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park - Adjacent to Shizu Shrine, featuring about 2,000 double-flowered cherry trees. == Notes == '''Annotations''' {{reflist|group="note"}} '''References''' {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine history document * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1982|chapter=|title={{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|publisher=[[Heibonsha]]|isbn=4582490085|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=「Shizu Village」|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=「Shizu Shrine」|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}}}。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[Kenichi Tanigawa]]|author=Katsumi Kitabatake|year=1984|chapter=Shizu Shrine|title=Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 11 Kanto|publisher=[[Hakusuisha]]|isbn=4560025118|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=Medieval Provincial Shrine Research Association|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=Fundamental Research on Medieval Provincial Shrine System|publisher=Iwata Shoin|page=45|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000}}}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shizu-jinja (Naka)}} * [https://shizu.e-naka.jp/index.html Hitachi Ninomiya Shizu Shrine] - Official website * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/201601.html Shizu Shrine] - Kokugakuin University's 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection" {{Shinto sidebar}} {{citation needed|Shizu Shrine}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Shizu Shrine]] {{citation needed|Shizu Shrine}} {{citation needed|Shizu Shrine}} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Shizu Shrine]][[simple:user:immanuelle/Shizu Shrine]] {{draft categories| }} {{Shizuri Faith}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shizuri Faith]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai-sha in Hitachi Province|Shizu Shrine]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Naka, Ibaraki]] [[Category:History of Naka, Ibaraki]] [[Category:Hitachi Province|Shrine 2]] [[Category:Ninomiya]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Shizu Shrine]] [[Category:New]] }} [[ja:静神社]] [[sn:Shizu Shrine]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Shizu Shrine}}

{{Otheruses| |京都府京丹後市にある神社|静神社 (京丹後市)}} {{神社 |名称 = 静神社 |画像 = [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[茨城県]][[那珂市]]静2 |位置 = {{Coord|36|30|6|N|140|25|20|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[天羽槌雄神|建葉槌命]] |神体 = |社格 = [[式内社]]（[[名神大社|名神大]]）
[[常陸国]][[一宮|二宮]]
旧[[県社]] |創建 = （伝）[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]） |本殿 = [[神明造]]銅板葺 |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[4月1日]] |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Ibaraki|label=静神社|coordinates= {{coord2|36|30|6|N|140|25|20|E|}}|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|30|6|N|140|25|20|E}}}} }} {{座標一覧}} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|一の鳥居}}]] '''静神社'''（しずじんじゃ）は、[[茨城県]][[那珂市]]静にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）、[[常陸国]][[一宮|二宮]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。[[神紋]]は「丸に桜」。 == 社名 == 『[[常陸国風土記]]』[[久慈郡]]の条には「静織（しどり）の里」とあり、上古に綾を織る機を知る人がここで初めて織ったのでその由来となったと見える{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。また、『[[和名類聚抄]]』には常陸国久慈郡に「倭文郷（しどりごう）」の記載があり{{Sfn|静村（平凡社）|1982年}}、これらの「シドリ」が縮まり「静（しず）」の地名・社名となったと推測される{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。加えて、『[[万葉集]]』には[[常陸国]]の住人である[[倭文部可良麻呂]]の名前が見え、[[倭文部]]が常陸国に居住していたことも推測できる。 なお、当地は現在では[[那珂郡]]地域に位置する。当地を含む[[久慈川]]以西は中世には久慈西郡であったが、[[太閤検地|文禄検地]]で那珂郡に編入されたという{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の4柱神社由緒書。。 ; 主祭神 :* [[天羽槌雄神|建葉槌命]]（たけはづちのみこと） - 別名を「倭文神（しどりのかみ）」とする。 ; 相殿神 :* [[アメノタヂカラオ|手力雄命]]（たぢからをのみこと） :* [[タカミムスビ|高皇産霊命]]（たかみむすびのみこと） :* [[オモイカネ|思兼命]]（おもいかねのみこと） === 祭神について === 主祭神の建葉槌命について、『[[古語拾遺]]』には「[[天羽槌雄神]]」と記載され、倭文の遠祖であり文布を織って[[天照大神]]に仕えたとある{{Sfn|静神社（平凡社）|1982年}}。また、『[[日本書紀]]』神代には「倭文神建葉槌命」とあり、[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌神]]・[[経津主神]]の[[葦原中国平定]]で従わなかった[[天津甕星|星神香香背男]]へ派遣されて平定したという{{Sfn|静神社（平凡社）|1982年}}。 なお、[[江戸時代]]末期までは手力男命（手力雄命）を主神としていた{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。『新編常陸国誌』によれば、その当時に祀られていた手力男命は小勝村から移祭したもので、古来から鎮まっていたのは天葉槌命（建葉槌命）であるという{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === 創建は不詳。『新編常陸国誌』では[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]）に創建されたという社伝を載せる{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 前述のように当地は倭文部、すなわち文様付の布を織る技術者集団の居住地と見られ、静神社はその関係社と見られている{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。また、静神社東方には5世紀を中心とした古墳群（新宿古墳群<あらじゅくこふんぐん>）が残っており、静神社との関係性が指摘される。 === 概史 === [[六国史|国史]]では、[[仁和]]元年（[[885年]]）に「静神」の[[神階]]が従五位上に昇叙されたと見える静神社の由緒書では『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）9月庚午条の「使を遣し静神社に奉幣せしむ」という記事があるとするが、詳細は明らかでない。。[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[常陸国]][[久慈郡]]に「静神社 名神大」と記載され、[[名神大社]]に列している。 また、[[鹿島神宮]]（一宮）や[[吉田神社 (水戸市)|吉田神社]]（三宮）とともに静神社は常陸国の二宮として崇敬されたというただし、これら一宮から三宮の近世の呼称は確認可能であるが、中世の文書による裏付けはされていない {{Harv|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=45}}。。このように崇敬された理由として、遅くとも[[奈良時代]]から麻布の使用が庶民に広がったが、常陸国はその特産地であり静神社がその生産に関与したためとする説がある{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 中世には[[佐竹氏]]が当地を領有し、[[佐竹貞義]]によって静神社境内に弘願寺・西方寺・静安寺が設けられた{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 江戸時代には、[[慶長]]7年（[[1602年]]）に[[徳川秀忠]]から神領150石が寄進された{{Sfn|静神社（平凡社）|1982年}}。その後は[[水戸徳川家]]の祈願所とされ、維持管理は藩費によってなされたという。[[寛文]]7年（[[1667年]]）に[[徳川光圀]]（水戸第2代）が社殿を修造し、弘願寺を含めて3寺は廃されたが、この際に銅印（重要文化財）が発見されている{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。これにより、[[神仏習合]]から[[吉田神道|唯一宗源神道]]に改められた。以後も徳川氏から崇敬され、[[徳川綱條]]（水戸第3代）からは三十六歌仙が奉納され、[[徳川斉昭]]（水戸第9代）が[[天保]]12年（[[1841年]]）の火災で焼失していた社殿を再建した{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。なお、その火災で燃えた神木の切り株は現在も境内にある。 [[明治]]に入り、[[近代社格制度]]では[[県社]]に列した。 === 神階 === * [[仁和]]元年（[[885年]]）5月22日、従五位下から従五位上 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「静神」。 == 境内 == 本殿・拝殿・楼門に代表される社殿は、天保年間（[[1830年]] - [[1844年]]）に徳川斉昭による再建である。また、境内には東京織物卸商業組合が寄進した「織姫」像があるほか、静神社の使いは白い機織り物が長くのびる様子を表した「白蛇」とされており、現在も織物との関係は深い。 File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|本殿 File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|神門 File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|二の鳥居と社叢 File:Orihime.jpg|織姫像 == 摂末社 == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|手接足尾神社}}]] * 手接足尾神社 *: 本殿裏手の山中にある末社。手足の健康を守護する神として、手差しや草履を納めて祈願する風習がある。 その他、境内には数社が鎮座する。 == 関係地 == * [[弘願寺]] *: 元静神社内にあった[[臨済宗]]の[[寺院]]で、徳川光圀により分離された。[[明治時代]]の[[廃仏毀釈]]により廃寺になったが、茨城県那珂市下大賀に再建された。 * 新宿古墳群 *: 境内東方にある古墳群。そのうち、権現塚古墳 （那珂市指定史跡、{{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=権現塚古墳}}）は墳丘長31メートルの[[前方後円墳]]で、5世紀末頃の築造と推定される[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html 権現塚古墳]（那珂市教育委員会）。。この古墳群は、静神社を祀った倭文部の墳墓と見られている「新宿古墳群」『日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名』 平凡社、1982年。。 == 祭事 == * 歳旦祭 （1月1日） * 節分祭 （節分の日） * 春の例祭 （4月1日） * 御田植祭 （6月5日） * 七五三祭 （11月15日） * 新穀感謝祭 （11月23日） * 織物祭 （11月25日） * 秋の大祭 （11月25日-27日） ** 宵祭 （11月25日） ** 本祭 （11月26日、27日） - 27日には特殊神事の蔦舞・お笹明神出御が行われる。 なお、古くは旧暦4月9日に「磯降り神事」として海岸まで神幸が行なわれていた{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 銅印（附 印笥）（考古資料） *: 奈良時代の作と見られる銅製の印。印面には「静神宮印」とある。[[寛文]]7年（[[1667年]]）、徳川光圀による社殿造営の際に境内から発掘された。黒塗りの箱（印笥）に納められ、箱には徳川光圀自身の手により金文字で「宰相中将水戸源臣光圀謹記」と記されている。昭和29年3月20日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9731|銅印〈印文「静神宮印」〉}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html 銅印(附印笥)]（那珂市教育委員会）。。 === 茨城県指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 紙本著色三十六歌仙 35枚（絵画） **: 江戸時代、水戸第3代藩主[[徳川綱條]]が[[宝永]]2年（[[1705年]]）に奉納したもの。[[天保]]12年（[[1841年]]）の火災で1枚は焼失。昭和37年10月24日指定[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html 紙本著色三十六歌仙]（那珂市教育委員会）。。 === 那珂市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 陣太鼓（工芸品） **: 直径146センチメートル、長さ61センチメートルの太鼓。江戸時代の天保11年（[[1840年]]）頃、徳川斉昭により追鳥狩用の軍鼓として作られた。平成15年7月17日指定[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html 陣太鼓]（那珂市教育委員会）。。 === その他 === * 「静神社」の掛け軸 - [[三条実美]][[公爵]]の書。 * 桜田門外の変の錦絵 - 静神社の神官の子で水戸藩士だった斎藤監物が[[桜田門外の変]]に参加した様子が描かれた[[錦絵]]。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[茨城県]][[那珂市]]静2 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道：[[東日本旅客鉄道]]（JR東日本）[[水郡線]] [[静駅]]から1.5km{{Cite book|和書 |title =週刊 JR全駅・全車両基地 |publisher = [[朝日新聞出版]] |series=週刊朝日百科 |volume =42号 水戸駅・常陸太田駅・高萩駅ほか74駅 |date =2013-06-09 |page =25 }} * 車：[[常磐自動車道]] [[那珂インターチェンジ|那珂IC]]から6km '''周辺''' * 静峰公園 - 静神社に隣接し、約2,000本の八重桜が植えられている。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} '''注釈''' {{reflist|group="注"}} '''出典''' {{reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * 神社由緒書 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1982|chapter=|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 8 茨城県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490085|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=「静村」|ref={{Harvid|静村（平凡社）|1982年}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=「静神社」|ref={{Harvid|静神社（平凡社）|1982年}}}}。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[谷川健一]]|author=北畠克美|year=1984|chapter=静神社|title=日本の神々 -神社と聖地- 11 関東|publisher=[[白水社]]|isbn=4560025118|ref={{Harvid|静神社（神々）|1984年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|page=45|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|中世諸国一宮制|2000年}}}} == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Shizu-jinja (Naka)}} * [https://shizu.e-naka.jp/index.html 常陸二ノ宮 静神社] - 公式サイト * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/201601.html 静神社] - 國學院大學21世紀COEプログラム「神道・神社史料集成」 {{神道 横}}{{茨城県の神社一覧目次}} {{DEFAULTSORT:しすしんしや}} [[Category:茨城県の神社]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:常陸国の式内社|名しすしんしや]] [[Category:茨城県の旧県社]] [[Category:茨城県の重要文化財]] [[Category:那珂市の建築物]] [[Category:那珂市の歴史]] [[Category:常陸国|社2]] [[Category:二宮]] [[Category:茨城百景]]

{{Otheruses| |京都府京丹後市にある神社|静神社 (京丹後市)}} {{神社 |名称 = 静神社 |画像 = [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[茨城県]][[那珂市]]静2 |位置 = {{Coord|36|30|6|N|140|25|20|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[天羽槌雄神|建葉槌命]] |神体 = |社格 = [[式内社]]（[[名神大社|名神大]]）
[[常陸国]][[一宮|二宮]]
旧[[県社]] |創建 = （伝）[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]） |本殿 = [[神明造]]銅板葺 |別名 = |札所等 = |例祭 = [[4月1日]] |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Ibaraki|label=静神社|coordinates= {{coord2|36|30|6|N|140|25|20|E|}}|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|30|6|N|140|25|20|E}}}} }} {{座標一覧}} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|一の鳥居}}]] '''静神社'''（しずじんじゃ）は、[[茨城県]][[那珂市]]静にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）、[[常陸国]][[一宮|二宮]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]。[[神紋]]は「丸に桜」。 == 社名 == 『[[常陸国風土記]]』[[久慈郡]]の条には「静織（しどり）の里」とあり、上古に綾を織る機を知る人がここで初めて織ったのでその由来となったと見える{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。また、『[[和名類聚抄]]』には常陸国久慈郡に「倭文郷（しどりごう）」の記載があり{{Sfn|静村（平凡社）|1982年}}、これらの「シドリ」が縮まり「静（しず）」の地名・社名となったと推測される{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。加えて、『[[万葉集]]』には[[常陸国]]の住人である[[倭文部可良麻呂]]の名前が見え、[[倭文部]]が常陸国に居住していたことも推測できる。 なお、当地は現在では[[那珂郡]]地域に位置する。当地を含む[[久慈川]]以西は中世には久慈西郡であったが、[[太閤検地|文禄検地]]で那珂郡に編入されたという{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の4柱神社由緒書。。 ; 主祭神 :* [[天羽槌雄神|建葉槌命]]（たけはづちのみこと） - 別名を「倭文神（しどりのかみ）」とする。 ; 相殿神 :* [[アメノタヂカラオ|手力雄命]]（たぢからをのみこと） :* [[タカミムスビ|高皇産霊命]]（たかみむすびのみこと） :* [[オモイカネ|思兼命]]（おもいかねのみこと） === 祭神について === 主祭神の建葉槌命について、『[[古語拾遺]]』には「[[天羽槌雄神]]」と記載され、倭文の遠祖であり文布を織って[[天照大神]]に仕えたとある{{Sfn|静神社（平凡社）|1982年}}。また、『[[日本書紀]]』神代には「倭文神建葉槌命」とあり、[[タケミカヅチ|武甕槌神]]・[[経津主神]]の[[葦原中国平定]]で従わなかった[[天津甕星|星神香香背男]]へ派遣されて平定したという{{Sfn|静神社（平凡社）|1982年}}。 なお、[[江戸時代]]末期までは手力男命（手力雄命）を主神としていた{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。『新編常陸国誌』によれば、その当時に祀られていた手力男命は小勝村から移祭したもので、古来から鎮まっていたのは天葉槌命（建葉槌命）であるという{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 == 歴史 == === 創建 === 創建は不詳。『新編常陸国誌』では[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]）に創建されたという社伝を載せる{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 前述のように当地は倭文部、すなわち文様付の布を織る技術者集団の居住地と見られ、静神社はその関係社と見られている{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。また、静神社東方には5世紀を中心とした古墳群（新宿古墳群<あらじゅくこふんぐん>）が残っており、静神社との関係性が指摘される。 === 概史 === [[六国史|国史]]では、[[仁和]]元年（[[885年]]）に「静神」の[[神階]]が従五位上に昇叙されたと見える静神社の由緒書では『日本文徳天皇実録』嘉祥3年（850年）9月庚午条の「使を遣し静神社に奉幣せしむ」という記事があるとするが、詳細は明らかでない。。[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[常陸国]][[久慈郡]]に「静神社 名神大」と記載され、[[名神大社]]に列している。 また、[[鹿島神宮]]（一宮）や[[吉田神社 (水戸市)|吉田神社]]（三宮）とともに静神社は常陸国の二宮として崇敬されたというただし、これら一宮から三宮の近世の呼称は確認可能であるが、中世の文書による裏付けはされていない {{Harv|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=45}}。。このように崇敬された理由として、遅くとも[[奈良時代]]から麻布の使用が庶民に広がったが、常陸国はその特産地であり静神社がその生産に関与したためとする説がある{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 中世には[[佐竹氏]]が当地を領有し、[[佐竹貞義]]によって静神社境内に弘願寺・西方寺・静安寺が設けられた{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 江戸時代には、[[慶長]]7年（[[1602年]]）に[[徳川秀忠]]から神領150石が寄進された{{Sfn|静神社（平凡社）|1982年}}。その後は[[水戸徳川家]]の祈願所とされ、維持管理は藩費によってなされたという。[[寛文]]7年（[[1667年]]）に[[徳川光圀]]（水戸第2代）が社殿を修造し、弘願寺を含めて3寺は廃されたが、この際に銅印（重要文化財）が発見されている{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。これにより、[[神仏習合]]から[[吉田神道|唯一宗源神道]]に改められた。以後も徳川氏から崇敬され、[[徳川綱條]]（水戸第3代）からは三十六歌仙が奉納され、[[徳川斉昭]]（水戸第9代）が[[天保]]12年（[[1841年]]）の火災で焼失していた社殿を再建した{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。なお、その火災で燃えた神木の切り株は現在も境内にある。 [[明治]]に入り、[[近代社格制度]]では[[県社]]に列した。 === 神階 === * [[仁和]]元年（[[885年]]）5月22日、従五位下から従五位上 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「静神」。 == 境内 == 本殿・拝殿・楼門に代表される社殿は、天保年間（[[1830年]] - [[1844年]]）に徳川斉昭による再建である。また、境内には東京織物卸商業組合が寄進した「織姫」像があるほか、静神社の使いは白い機織り物が長くのびる様子を表した「白蛇」とされており、現在も織物との関係は深い。 File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|本殿 File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|神門 File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|二の鳥居と社叢 File:Orihime.jpg|織姫像 == 摂末社 == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|手接足尾神社}}]] * 手接足尾神社 *: 本殿裏手の山中にある末社。手足の健康を守護する神として、手差しや草履を納めて祈願する風習がある。 その他、境内には数社が鎮座する。 == 関係地 == * [[弘願寺]] *: 元静神社内にあった[[臨済宗]]の[[寺院]]で、徳川光圀により分離された。[[明治時代]]の[[廃仏毀釈]]により廃寺になったが、茨城県那珂市下大賀に再建された。 * 新宿古墳群 *: 境内東方にある古墳群。そのうち、権現塚古墳 （那珂市指定史跡、{{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=権現塚古墳}}）は墳丘長31メートルの[[前方後円墳]]で、5世紀末頃の築造と推定される[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html 権現塚古墳]（那珂市教育委員会）。。この古墳群は、静神社を祀った倭文部の墳墓と見られている「新宿古墳群」『日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名』 平凡社、1982年。。 == 祭事 == * 歳旦祭 （1月1日） * 節分祭 （節分の日） * 春の例祭 （4月1日） * 御田植祭 （6月5日） * 七五三祭 （11月15日） * 新穀感謝祭 （11月23日） * 織物祭 （11月25日） * 秋の大祭 （11月25日-27日） ** 宵祭 （11月25日） ** 本祭 （11月26日、27日） - 27日には特殊神事の蔦舞・お笹明神出御が行われる。 なお、古くは旧暦4月9日に「磯降り神事」として海岸まで神幸が行なわれていた{{Sfn|静神社（神々）|1984年}}。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財（国指定） === * 銅印（附 印笥）（考古資料） *: 奈良時代の作と見られる銅製の印。印面には「静神宮印」とある。[[寛文]]7年（[[1667年]]）、徳川光圀による社殿造営の際に境内から発掘された。黒塗りの箱（印笥）に納められ、箱には徳川光圀自身の手により金文字で「宰相中将水戸源臣光圀謹記」と記されている。昭和29年3月20日指定{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9731|銅印〈印文「静神宮印」〉}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html 銅印(附印笥)]（那珂市教育委員会）。。 === 茨城県指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 紙本著色三十六歌仙 35枚（絵画） **: 江戸時代、水戸第3代藩主[[徳川綱條]]が[[宝永]]2年（[[1705年]]）に奉納したもの。[[天保]]12年（[[1841年]]）の火災で1枚は焼失。昭和37年10月24日指定[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html 紙本著色三十六歌仙]（那珂市教育委員会）。。 === 那珂市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財 ** 陣太鼓（工芸品） **: 直径146センチメートル、長さ61センチメートルの太鼓。江戸時代の天保11年（[[1840年]]）頃、徳川斉昭により追鳥狩用の軍鼓として作られた。平成15年7月17日指定[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html 陣太鼓]（那珂市教育委員会）。。 === その他 === * 「静神社」の掛け軸 - [[三条実美]][[公爵]]の書。 * 桜田門外の変の錦絵 - 静神社の神官の子で水戸藩士だった斎藤監物が[[桜田門外の変]]に参加した様子が描かれた[[錦絵]]。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[茨城県]][[那珂市]]静2 '''交通アクセス''' * 鉄道：[[東日本旅客鉄道]]（JR東日本）[[水郡線]] [[静駅]]から1.5km{{Cite book|和書 |title =週刊 JR全駅・全車両基地 |publisher = [[朝日新聞出版]] |series=週刊朝日百科 |volume =42号 水戸駅・常陸太田駅・高萩駅ほか74駅 |date =2013-06-09 |page =25 }} * 車：[[常磐自動車道]] [[那珂インターチェンジ|那珂IC]]から6km '''周辺''' * 静峰公園 - It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and the second shrine ({{ill|Ninomiya|ja|二宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) of {{ill|Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, with the old shrine Rank of {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine crest is "circle with cherry blossoms." == Shrine name == In the section on {{ill|Kuji District, Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the {{ill|Fudoki|ja|風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is mentioned as "Shidorino Sato," named after the people who first wove textiles there in ancient times {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, the {{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|ja|和名類聚抄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} mentions "Shidorigo" in Kuji District, Hitachi Province {{Sfn|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}, and it is speculated that "Shidori" was shortened to "Shizu" as the name of the place and shrine {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Moreover, the {{ill|Man'yōshū|ja|万葉集|qq=draft|qq=draft}} mentions a resident of Hitachi Province, {{ill|Shitateru Karasumaro|ja|倭文部可良麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, suggesting that the Shitateru people lived in Hitachi Province. Currently, the area is part of the Naka District. The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|ja|アメノタヂカラオ|translation=Tejikarao no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} :* {{ill|Takami Musubi|ja|タカミムスビ|1=Takamimusubi|translation=Takami Musubi no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} :* {{ill|Omoikane|ja|オモイカネ|translation=Omoikane no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft}} === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古語拾遺|qq=draft|qq=draft}} records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀|qq=draft|qq=draft}} records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|タケミカヅチ|translation=Takemikazuchi no Kami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Futsunushi no Kami|ja|経津主神|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity {{ill|Amatsu-Mikaboshi|ja|天津甕星|1=Amatsu-Mikaboshi|2=zh|3=天津甕星|4=ja|5=天津甕星|6=ru|7=Амацумикабоси|8=tr|9=Amatsu Mikaboşi|10=mni|11=ꯑꯃꯠꯁꯨ-ꯃꯤꯀꯕꯣꯁꯤ|12=th|13=อามัตสึมิกาโบชิ|15=draft|translation=Hoshikagaseo no Kami|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. The {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft}} states that the shrine was founded in the 1st year of the Daido era (806 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. As mentioned earlier, the area was inhabited by the Shitateru people, a group of weavers specializing in patterned textiles, and Shizu Shrine is thought to be related to them {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the {{ill|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. The {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s list of shrines, compiled in the 5th year of the Engi era (927 AD), includes Shizu Shrine as a Myōjin Taisha in Kuji District, Hitachi Province. Shizu Shrine, along with {{ill|Kashima Shrine|ja|鹿島神宮|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the first shrine) and {{ill|Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|ja|吉田神社 (水戸市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (the third shrine), was revered as the second shrine of Hitachi Province While the designations of first through third shrines can be confirmed in modern times, there is no documentary evidence from the Middle Ages to support this claim {{Harv|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000|p=45}}.. One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the {{ill|Satake clan|ja|佐竹氏|qq=draft|qq=draft}} ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|qq=draft|qq=draft}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from {{ill|Tokugawa Hidetada|ja|徳川秀忠|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the {{ill|Mito-Tokugawa family|ja|水戸徳川家|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), {{ill|Tokugawa Mitsukuni|ja|徳川光圀|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the {{ill|Yoshida Shinto|ja|吉田神道|translation=Sole Original Shinto|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch. {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Shrine Ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ({{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by {{ill|Tokugawa Nariaki|ja|徳川斉昭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by {{ill|Sanjō Sanetomi|ja|三条実美|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * {{ill|Naka, Ibaraki|ja|那珂市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Shizu 2, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|ja|茨城県|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from {{ill|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|ja|静駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Suigun Line|ja|水郡線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|ja|東日本旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Jōban Expressway|ja|常磐自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park -
