One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the [[:en:Satake clan|Satake clan]] ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satake Yoshinobu|qq=}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from [[:en:Tokugawa Hidetada|Tokugawa Hidetada]] in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the [[:en:Mito Tokugawa family|Mito-Tokugawa family]], and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), [[:en:Tokugawa Mitsukuni|Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]]. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch. [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]], the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Shrine Ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]] during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|qq=}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by [[:en:Sanjō Sanetomi|Sanjō Sanetomi]], a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]] Shizu 2, [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]] '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from [[:en:Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)]], [[:en:Suigun Line|Suigun Line]], [[:en:East Japan Railway Company|East Japan Railway Company]] * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naka Interchange|qq=}}, [[:en:Jōban Expressway|Jōban Expressway]] '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park - Adjacent to Shizu Shrine, featuring about 2,000 double-flowered cherry trees. == Notes == '''Annotations''' {{reflist|group="note"}} '''References''' {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine history document * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1982|chapter=|title={{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|qq=}}|publisher=[[Heibonsha]]|isbn=4582490085|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=「Shizu Village」|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=「Shizu Shrine」|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}}}。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[Kenichi Tanigawa]]|author=Katsumi Kitabatake|year=1984|chapter=Shizu Shrine|title=Japanese Gods - Shrines and Sacred Places - 11 Kanto|publisher=[[Hakusuisha]]|isbn=4560025118|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=Medieval Provincial Shrine Research Association|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=Fundamental Research on Medieval Provincial Shrine System|publisher=Iwata Shoin|page=45|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000}}}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Shizu-jinja (Naka)}} * [https://shizu.e-naka.jp/index.html Hitachi Ninomiya Shizu Shrine] - Official website * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/201601.html Shizu Shrine] - Kokugakuin University's 21st Century COE Program "Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection" {{Shinto sidebar}} {{Shizuri Faith}} {{translated page|ja|静神社|version=101958783|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Shizuri Faith]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province|Shizu Shrine]] [[Category:Prefectural shrines in Ibaraki Prefecture]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Naka, Ibaraki]] [[Category:History of Naka, Ibaraki]] [[Category:Hitachi Province|Shrine 2]] [[Category:Ninomiya]] [[Category:Ibaraki 100 Landscapes]] [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Shizu Shrine]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Shizu Shrine]][[Category:qq]] }} [[simple:user:immanuelle/Shizu Shrine]] [[ja:静神社]] [[sn:Shizu Shrine]] [[sn:Shizu Shrine]] [[Category:二宮]] [[Category:Hitachi Province]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Hitachi Province]] [[Category:茨城百景]] [[Category:茨城県の旧県社]]

Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}} | founded = (Tradition) [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido (era)]] 1st year ({{ill|806|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/806|qq=}} AD)|main_building = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] copper roofing | other_names = | pilgrimage_sites = | annual_festival = [[:en:April 1|April 1st]] | ceremonies = | map = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Shizu Shrine''' (静神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]], [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=}}) and the second shrine ([[:en:Ninomiya|Ninomiya]]) of [[:en:Hitachi Province|Hitachi Province]], with the old shrine Rank of {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}}. The shrine crest is "circle with cherry blossoms." == Shrine name == In the section on {{ill|Kuji District, Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuji District, Hitachi Province|qq=}} in the [[:en:Fudoki|Fudoki]], it is mentioned as "Shidorino Sato," named after the people who first wove textiles there in ancient times {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Wamyō Ruijushō|Wamyō Ruijushō]] mentions "Shidorigo" in Kuji District, Hitachi Province {{Sfn|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}, and it is speculated that "Shidori" was shortened to "Shizu" as the name of the place and shrine {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Moreover, the [[:en:Man'yōshū|Man'yōshū]] mentions a resident of Hitachi Province, {{ill|Shitateru Karasumaro|ja|倭文部可良麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateru Karasumaro|qq=}}, suggesting that the Shitateru people lived in Hitachi Province. Currently, the area is part of the Naka District. The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahazuchi no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] :* [[:en:Takamimusubi|Takamimusubi]] :* [[:en:Omoikane|Omoikane]] === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the [[:en:Kogo Shūi|Kojiki]] records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]] and [[:en:Futsunushi|Futsunushi no Kami]], he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity [[:en:Amatsu-Mikaboshi|Amatsu-Mikaboshi]] {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. The {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=}} states that the shrine was founded in the 1st year of the Daido era (806 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. As mentioned earlier, the area was inhabited by the Shitateru people, a group of weavers specializing in patterned textiles, and Shizu Shrine is thought to be related to them {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank|qq=}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the [[:en:Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku]] in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. [[:en:Hitachi Province|Hitachi Province]] [[:en:Ninomiya|Ninomiya]]
Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}} | founded = (Tradition) [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido (era)]] 1st year ({{ill|806|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/806|qq=}} AD)|main_building = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] copper roofing | other_names = | pilgrimage_sites = | annual_festival = [[:en:April 1|April 1st]] | ceremonies = | map = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Shizu Shrine''' (静神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]], [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=}}) and the second shrine ([[:en:Ninomiya|Ninomiya]]) of [[:en:Hitachi Province|Hitachi Province]], with the old shrine Rank of {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}}. The shrine crest is "circle with cherry blossoms." == Shrine name == In the section on {{ill|Kuji District, Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuji District, Hitachi Province|qq=}} in the [[:en:Fudoki|Fudoki]], it is mentioned as "Shidorino Sato," named after the people who first wove textiles there in ancient times {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Wamyō Ruijushō|Wamyō Ruijushō]] mentions "Shidorigo" in Kuji District, Hitachi Province {{Sfn|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}, and it is speculated that "Shidori" was shortened to "Shizu" as the name of the place and shrine {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Moreover, the [[:en:Man'yōshū|Man'yōshū]] mentions a resident of Hitachi Province, {{ill|Shitateru Karasumaro|ja|倭文部可良麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateru Karasumaro|qq=}}, suggesting that the Shitateru people lived in Hitachi Province. Currently, the area is part of the Naka District. The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahazuchi no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] :* [[:en:Takamimusubi|Takamimusubi]] :* [[:en:Omoikane|Omoikane]] === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the [[:en:Kogo Shūi|Kojiki]] records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]] and [[:en:Futsunushi|Futsunushi no Kami]], he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity [[:en:Amatsu-Mikaboshi|Amatsu-Mikaboshi]] {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. The {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=}} states that the shrine was founded in the 1st year of the Daido era (806 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. As mentioned earlier, the area was inhabited by the Shitateru people, a group of weavers specializing in patterned textiles, and Shizu Shrine is thought to be related to them {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank|qq=}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the [[:en:Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku]] in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]'s list of shrines, compiled in the 5th year of the Engi era (927 AD), includes Shizu Shrine as a Myōjin Taisha in Kuji District, Hitachi Province. Shizu Shrine, along with [[:en:Kashima Shrine|Kashima Shrine]] (the first shrine) and {{ill|Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|ja|吉田神社 (水戸市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|qq=}} (the third shrine), was revered as the second shrine of Hitachi Province While the designations of first through third shrines can be confirmed in modern times, there is no documentary evidence from the Middle Ages to support this claim {{Harv|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000|p=45}}.. One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the [[:en:Satake clan|Satake clan]] ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satake Yoshinobu|qq=}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from [[:en:Tokugawa Hidetada|Tokugawa Hidetada]] in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the [[:en:Mito Tokugawa family|Mito-Tokugawa family]], and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), [[:en:Tokugawa Mitsukuni|Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]]. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch. [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]], the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Shrine Ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]] during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|qq=}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by [[:en:Sanjō Sanetomi|Sanjō Sanetomi]], a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]] Shizu 2, [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]] '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from [[:en:Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)]], [[:en:Suigun Line|Suigun Line]], [[:en:East Japan Railway Company|East Japan Railway Company]] * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naka Interchange|qq=}}, [[:en:Jōban Expressway|Jōban Expressway]] '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park - Adjacent to Shizu Shrine, featuring about 2,000 double-flowered cherry trees. == Notes == '''Annotations''' {{reflist|group="note"}} '''References''' {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * Shrine history document * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1982|chapter=|title={{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|qq=}}|publisher=[[Heibonsha]]|isbn=4582490085|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=「Shizu Village」|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=「Shizu Shrine」|ref={{Harvid|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}}}。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=[[Kenichi Tanigawa]]|author=Katsumi Kitabatake|year=1984|chapter=Shizu Shrine|title=Japanese Gods - Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}} | founded = (Tradition) [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido (era)]] 1st year ({{ill|806|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/806|qq=}} AD)|main_building = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] copper roofing | other_names = | pilgrimage_sites = | annual_festival = [[:en:April 1|April 1st]] | ceremonies = | map = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Shizu Shrine''' (静神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]], [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=}}) and the second shrine ([[:en:Ninomiya|Ninomiya]]) of [[:en:Hitachi Province|Hitachi Province]], with the old shrine Rank of {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=}}. The shrine crest is "circle with cherry blossoms." == Shrine name == In the section on {{ill|Kuji District, Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuji District, Hitachi Province|qq=}} in the [[:en:Fudoki|Fudoki]], it is mentioned as "Shidorino Sato," named after the people who first wove textiles there in ancient times {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Wamyō Ruijushō|Wamyō Ruijushō]] mentions "Shidorigo" in Kuji District, Hitachi Province {{Sfn|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}, and it is speculated that "Shidori" was shortened to "Shizu" as the name of the place and shrine {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Moreover, the [[:en:Man'yōshū|Man'yōshū]] mentions a resident of Hitachi Province, {{ill|Shitateru Karasumaro|ja|倭文部可良麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateru Karasumaro|qq=}}, suggesting that the Shitateru people lived in Hitachi Province. Currently, the area is part of the Naka District. The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahazuchi no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] :* [[:en:Takamimusubi|Takamimusubi]] :* [[:en:Omoikane|Omoikane]] === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the [[:en:Kogo Shūi|Kojiki]] records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]] and [[:en:Futsunushi|Futsunushi no Kami]], he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity [[:en:Amatsu-Mikaboshi|Amatsu-Mikaboshi]] {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. The {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=}} states that the shrine was founded in the 1st year of the Daido era (806 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. As mentioned earlier, the area was inhabited by the Shitateru people, a group of weavers specializing in patterned textiles, and Shizu Shrine is thought to be related to them {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank|qq=}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the [[:en:Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku]] in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]'s list of shrines, compiled in the 5th year of the Engi era (927 AD), includes Shizu Shrine as a Myōjin Taisha in Kuji District, Hitachi Province. Shizu Shrine, along with [[:en:Kashima Shrine|Kashima Shrine]] (the first shrine) and {{ill|Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|ja|吉田神社 (水戸市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|qq=}} (the third shrine), was revered as the second shrine of Hitachi Province While the designations of first through third shrines can be confirmed in modern times, there is no documentary evidence from the Middle Ages to support this claim {{Harv|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000|p=45}}.. One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the [[:en:Satake clan|Satake clan]] ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satake Yoshinobu|qq=}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from [[:en:Tokugawa Hidetada|Tokugawa Hidetada]] in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the [[:en:Mito Tokugawa family|Mito-Tokugawa family]], and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), [[:en:Tokugawa Mitsukuni|Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]]. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch. [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]], the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Shrine Ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]] during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|qq=}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by [[:en:Sanjō Sanetomi|Sanjō Sanetomi]], a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]] Shizu 2, [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]] '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from [[:en:Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)]], [[:en:Suigun Line|Suigun Line]], [[:en:East Japan Railway Company|East Japan Railway Company]] * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naka Interchange|qq=}}, [[:en:Jōban Expressway|Jōban Expressway]] '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park - Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank|qq=}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the [[:en:Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku]] in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]'s list of shrines, compiled in the 5th year of the Engi era (927 AD), includes Shizu Shrine as a Myōjin Taisha in Kuji District, Hitachi Province. Shizu Shrine, along with [[:en:Kashima Shrine|Kashima Shrine]] (the first shrine) and {{ill|Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|ja|吉田神社 (水戸市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|qq=}} (the third shrine), was revered as the second shrine of Hitachi Province While the designations of first through third shrines can be confirmed in modern times, there is no documentary evidence from the Middle Ages to support this claim {{Harv|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000|p=45}}.. One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the [[:en:Satake clan|Satake clan]] ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satake Yoshinobu|qq=}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from [[:en:Tokugawa Hidetada|Tokugawa Hidetada]] in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the [[:en:Mito Tokugawa family|Mito-Tokugawa family]], and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), [[:en:Tokugawa Mitsukuni|Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]]. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch. [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]], the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Shrine Ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]] during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles. File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shinmon.JPG|Shrine Gate File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) shasou.JPG|Second Torii and Shrine Forest File:Orihime.jpg|Orihime Statue == Auxiliary and Branch Shrines == [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) Tetsugi-ashio-jinja.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Tesugiashio Shrine}}]] * Tesugiashio Shrine *: A branch shrine located in the mountains behind the main hall. It is believed to protect the health of hands and feet, and there is a custom of offering gloves and sandals for prayer. Several other small shrines are located within the grounds. == Related Sites == * Kōgan-ji *: A former Zen Buddhist temple that was part of Shizu Shrine, separated by Tokugawa Mitsukuni. It was abolished during the anti-Buddhist movement of the Meiji era but was rebuilt in Shimooga, Naka City, Ibaraki Prefecture. * Shinjuku Kofun Cluster *: An ancient Kofun cluster located east of the shrine. The main mound, Gongen-zuka Kofun (a designated historical site in Naka City, {{Coord|36|30|30.08|N|140|25|31.98|E|region:JP-08_type:landmark|name=Gongen-zuka Kofun}}), is a keyhole-shaped Kofun with a length of 31 meters, estimated to have been built in the late 5th century [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000641.html Gongen-zuka Kofun] (Naka City Board of Education).. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|qq=}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. In ancient times, there was a procession to the coast for the "Iso Oriri" ritual on the old lunar calendar date of April 9th {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (Nationally Designated) === * Copper Seal (with Seal Box) (Archaeological Material) *: A copper seal believed to have been made during the Nara period. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. Designated on March 20, 1954 {{National Cultural Properties Database|201|9731|Copper Seal "Shizu Jingu Seal"}}[http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000591.html Copper Seal (with Seal Box)] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Ibaraki Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry, 35 scrolls (Paintings) **: Donated by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch, in the 2nd year of the Hoei era (1705 AD). One scroll was lost in the fire of the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD). Designated on October 24, 1962 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000592.html Illustrated Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Naka City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** War Drum (Craft) **: A drum with a diameter of 146 cm and a length of 61 cm, created as a military drum for falconry in the 11th year of the Tenpō era (1840 AD) by Tokugawa Nariaki. Designated on July 17, 2003 [http://www.city.naka.lg.jp/page/page000624.html War Drum] (Naka City Board of Education).. === Others === * Hanging Scroll with "Shizu Shrine" - Calligraphy by [[:en:Sanjō Sanetomi|Sanjō Sanetomi]], a duke. * Woodblock Print of the Sakuradamon Incident - A woodblock print depicting the participation of Saito Kanemono, a Mito clan samurai and son of a Shizu Shrine priest, in the Sakuradamon Incident. == Local Information == '''location''' * [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]] Shizu 2, [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]] '''Access''' * Train: 1.5 km from [[:en:Shizu Station (Ibaraki)|Shizu Station (Ibaraki)]], [[:en:Suigun Line|Suigun Line]], [[:en:East Japan Railway Company|East Japan Railway Company]] * Car: 6 km from {{ill|Naka Interchange|ja|那珂インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naka Interchange|qq=}}, [[:en:Jōban Expressway|Jōban Expressway]] '''Nearby''' * Shizumine Park - Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | founded = (Tradition) [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido (era)]] 1st year ({{ill|806|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/806|qq=}} AD)|main_building = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] copper roofing | other_names = | pilgrimage_sites = | annual_festival = [[:en:April 1|April 1st]] | ceremonies = | map = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Shizu Shrine''' (静神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]], [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}) and the second shrine ([[:en:Ninomiya|Ninomiya]]) of [[:en:Hitachi Province|Hitachi Province]], with the old shrine Rank of {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine crest is "circle with cherry blossoms." == Shrine name == In the section on {{ill|Kuji District, Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuji District, Hitachi Province|qq=}} in the [[:en:Fudoki|Fudoki]], it is mentioned as "Shidorino Sato," named after the people who first wove textiles there in ancient times {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Wamyō Ruijushō|Wamyō Ruijushō]] mentions "Shidorigo" in Kuji District, Hitachi Province {{Sfn|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}, and it is speculated that "Shidori" was shortened to "Shizu" as the name of the place and shrine {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Moreover, the [[:en:Man'yōshū|Man'yōshū]] mentions a resident of Hitachi Province, {{ill|Shitateru Karasumaro|ja|倭文部可良麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateru Karasumaro|qq=}}, suggesting that the Shitateru people lived in Hitachi Province. Currently, the area is part of the Naka District. The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahazuchi no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] :* [[:en:Takamimusubi|Takamimusubi]] :* [[:en:Omoikane|Omoikane]] === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the [[:en:Kogo Shūi|Kojiki]] records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]] and [[:en:Futsunushi|Futsunushi no Kami]], he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity [[:en:Amatsu-Mikaboshi|Amatsu-Mikaboshi]] {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. This Kofun cluster is considered to be the tombs of the Shitateru people who enshrined Shizu Shrine "Shinjuku Kofun Cluster" {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|ja|日本歴史地名大系 8 茨城県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 8 Ibaraki-ken no Chimei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Heibonsha, 1982.. == festivals == * New Year's festival (January 1st) * Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day) * Spring festival (April 1st) * Rice Planting festival (June 5th) * Shichi-Go-San festival (November 15th) * New Harvest Thanksgiving festival (November 23rd) * Textile festival (November 25th) * Autumn Grand festival (November 25th-27th) ** Eve festival (November 25th) ** Main festival (November 26th, 27th) - Special ceremonies include the Tsutamai and the departure of the Osasa Myojin on the 27th. The seal face bears the inscription "Shizu Jingu Seal." It was excavated from the shrine grounds during Tokugawa Mitsukuni's reconstruction in the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD). The black lacquered box containing the seal has gold lettering inscribed by Tokugawa Mitsukuni himself. [[:en:Hitachi Province|Hitachi Province]] [[:en:Ninomiya|Ninomiya]]
Former {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} | founded = (Tradition) [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido (era)]] 1st year ({{ill|806|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/806|qq=}} AD)|main_building = [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] copper roofing | other_names = | pilgrimage_sites = | annual_festival = [[:en:April 1|April 1st]] | ceremonies = | map = Japan Ibaraki }} [[File:Shizu-jinja (Naka) ootorii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Shizu Shrine''' (静神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Naka, Ibaraki|Naka, Ibaraki]], [[:en:Ibaraki Prefecture|Ibaraki Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myōjin Taisha|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}) and the second shrine ([[:en:Ninomiya|Ninomiya]]) of [[:en:Hitachi Province|Hitachi Province]], with the old shrine Rank of {{ill|Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Prefectural shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. The shrine crest is "circle with cherry blossoms." == Shrine name == In the section on {{ill|Kuji District, Hitachi Province|ja|常陸国風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuji District, Hitachi Province|qq=}} in the [[:en:Fudoki|Fudoki]], it is mentioned as "Shidorino Sato," named after the people who first wove textiles there in ancient times {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Wamyō Ruijushō|Wamyō Ruijushō]] mentions "Shidorigo" in Kuji District, Hitachi Province {{Sfn|Shizu Village (Heibonsha)|1982}}, and it is speculated that "Shidori" was shortened to "Shizu" as the name of the place and shrine {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Moreover, the [[:en:Man'yōshū|Man'yōshū]] mentions a resident of Hitachi Province, {{ill|Shitateru Karasumaro|ja|倭文部可良麻呂|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shitateru Karasumaro|qq=}}, suggesting that the Shitateru people lived in Hitachi Province. Currently, the area is part of the Naka District. The area west of the Kuji River, including the shrine site, was once known as Kuji Nishigori in the Middle Ages, but was incorporated into the Naka District during the Bunroku Survey {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == Deities == The shrine enshrines the following four deitiesShrine history document.. ; Main deity :* {{ill|Takahazuchi no Mikoto|ja|天羽槌雄神|1=Takehazuchi|2=ja|3=天羽槌雄神|4=zh|5=天羽槌雄神|6=fr|7=Takehazuchi|lt=Takehazuchi|translation=Takehazuchi no Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takahazuchi no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Takehazuchi|qq=}} - Also known as "Shidori no Kami." ; Associated deities :* [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] :* [[:en:Takamimusubi|Takamimusubi]] :* [[:en:Omoikane|Omoikane]] === About the Deities === Regarding the main deity Takehazuchi no Mikoto, the [[:en:Kogo Shūi|Kojiki]] records him as "Ame no Hiwashi no Kami," stating that he is the distant ancestor of the Shitateru people who served [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] by weaving textiles {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Additionally, the [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that during the pacification of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni by [[:en:Takemikazuchi|Takemikazuchi]] and [[:en:Futsunushi|Futsunushi no Kami]], he was dispatched to subdue the rebellious star deity [[:en:Amatsu-Mikaboshi|Amatsu-Mikaboshi]] {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. Until the late Edo period, Tejikarao no Mikoto was the main deity {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. According to the {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the Tejikarao no Mikoto enshrined at that time was transferred from Kogamura, while Takehazuchi no Mikoto was the original deity worshipped there {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. == History == === Founding === The founding date is unknown. The {{ill|Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|ja|新編常陸国誌|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinpen Hitachi Fudoki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} states that the shrine was founded in the 1st year of the Daido era (806 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. As mentioned earlier, the area was inhabited by the Shitateru people, a group of weavers specializing in patterned textiles, and Shizu Shrine is thought to be related to them {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. Additionally, there is a cluster of ancient Kofuns (Shinjuku Kofun Cluster) from the 5th century near the shrine, suggesting a connection {{ref name="Shinjuku"}}. == Overview == According to historical records, in the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), the shrine was elevated to the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|ja|従五位上|1=Junior Fifth Rank|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Fifth Rank|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従五位}} The shrine history document mentions an article from the [[:en:Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Nihon Montoku Tenno Jitsuroku]] in which offerings were made to Shizu Shrine in the 3rd year of the Kasho era (850 AD), but the details are unclear.. The [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]]'s list of shrines, compiled in the 5th year of the Engi era (927 AD), includes Shizu Shrine as a Myōjin Taisha in Kuji District, Hitachi Province. Shizu Shrine, along with [[:en:Kashima Shrine|Kashima Shrine]] (the first shrine) and {{ill|Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|ja|吉田神社 (水戸市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida Shrine (Mito)|qq=}} (the third shrine), was revered as the second shrine of Hitachi Province While the designations of first through third shrines can be confirmed in modern times, there is no documentary evidence from the Middle Ages to support this claim {{Harv|Medieval Research on Provincial Shrines|2000|p=45}}.. One theory suggests that the spread of hemp cloth among the common people by the Nara period and Hitachi Province's role as a production center contributed to the shrine's veneration {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. During the Middle Ages, the [[:en:Satake clan|Satake clan]] ruled the area, and {{ill|Satake Yoshinobu|ja|佐竹義宣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Satake Yoshinobu|qq=}} established Kōgan-ji, Saihō-ji, and Shizuan-ji within the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In the Edo period, the shrine received a donation of 150 koku of land from [[:en:Tokugawa Hidetada|Tokugawa Hidetada]] in the 7th year of the Keichō era (1602 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1982}}. The shrine became a place of prayer for the [[:en:Mito Tokugawa family|Mito-Tokugawa family]], and its maintenance was funded by the domain. In the 7th year of the Kanbun era (1667 AD), [[:en:Tokugawa Mitsukuni|Tokugawa Mitsukuni]], the second head of the Mito branch of the Tokugawa family, rebuilt the shrine buildings and abolished the three temples within the grounds. During this reconstruction, a copper seal (an important cultural property) was discovered {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine was subsequently converted from a mixture of Shinto and Buddhism to the exclusive worship of the [[:en:Yoshida Shintō|Yoshida Shinto]]. The Tokugawa family continued to revere the shrine, and offerings such as the Thirty-Six Immortals of Poetry were made by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunaeda|ja|徳川綱條|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokugawa Tsunaeda|qq=}}, the third head of the Mito branch. [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]], the ninth head of the Mito branch, rebuilt the shrine after it was destroyed by fire in the 12th year of the Tenpō era (1841 AD) {{Sfn|Shizu Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The burned stump of the sacred tree remains on the shrine grounds. In the Meiji period, the shrine was Ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern shrine Ranking system. === Shrine Ranking === * In the 1st year of the Ninna era (885 AD), on May 22nd, the shrine was elevated from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade ([[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) - listed as "Shizu Shrine." == Shrine Grounds == The main hall, haiden, and romon gate were rebuilt by [[:en:Tokugawa Nariaki|Tokugawa Nariaki]] during the Tenpō era (1830-1844) . The shrine grounds include a statue of Orihime, donated by the Tokyo Textile Wholesalers Association. The shrine messenger is said to be a white snake, symbolizing the extension of white woven fabric, indicating the shrine's deep connection to textiles.
